text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government of Punjab province has imposed agriculture tax to be charged in varying categories depending upon the size of landholding and the nature of its irrigation, said an official handout.
- Two unidentified gunmen shot dead a Shi'ite Moslem activist in Lahore.

- All flour mills in the North Western Frontier Province will be closed down from May 5 for an indefinite period if compensation to a mill burnt down by a mob on Tuesday is not paid by the government, the NWFP Flour Mills Association said.
- President Farooq Leghari and Chinese Premier Li Peng discussed in Beijing prospects of Chinese technical support for setting up "mini or medium sized" hydroelectric power projects in Pakistan.
- Total assets of the Fauji Foundation have touched the eight billion rupees mark.

- Federal Minister for Water and Power and Incharge minister for Petroleum and Natural Resources Nisar Ali Khan said the government will announce an integrated plan in the next few weeks to get the electricity and gas companies out of their financial crisis.

- The Confederation of National Associations of Tanners of the European Union has threatened to invoke trade barrier regulations against Pakistan if it does not lift the restrictions on export of hides and skins.
